findings.detail: Criticality 7/10. The recursive prompt fixture checks only that a nested diff command appears; existing historical-guidance tests exercise a single repository. No test supplies distinct historical child instructions, so root-only guide lookup omits module/AGENTS.md while all prompt assertions pass. This retains the known historical-child-guidance issue under the explicit disposition to record it without fixing.
findings.fix: Preserve the current disposition. When the follow-up is authorized, add child and nested historical-guide fixtures that distinguish the trusted parent gitlink revision from current checkout instructions.
findings.title: write-scrut-tests: Structured output checks omit historical child guidance.

strengths: Consumer integration checks compare stored digest membership with prompts, validation, changes, gates and symlink discovery.
Corrected negative fixtures isolate inventory validation, and deterministic mutation coverage checks recursive collection consistency.
Write-failure fixtures require unsuccessful exit and empty output, including when later children could otherwise conceal failure.
Regression cases cover precise gitlink membership, unrelated-file rejection, nested edits, missing objects and symlink boundaries.
summary: Reviewed the complete committed scope against added and existing tests. No new Important or Critical coverage gaps were found; the known historical-child-guidance issue remains recorded without a change request. Runtime suites were not executed because their fixtures create files.
